corrections.was: A Title card is a full-screen card carrying the film's name, shown briefly at the start and at the end. Here it reads Walker Jumpman, a walkthrough. It takes six seconds of eighty-two, about seven percent, the shortest beat of the film. For example, a student opens the film of their dungeon game with a dark card naming the game, and shows the same card again for a moment at the very end.
corrections.now: A Title card is a full-screen card carrying the film's name, shown briefly at the start and at the end. Here it reads Walker Jumpman, a walkthrough. In this made-up film it takes six seconds of eighty-two, about seven percent, the shortest beat of the film. For example, a student opens the film of their dungeon game with a dark card naming the game, and shows the same card again for a moment at the very end.
corrections.why: The six seconds of eighty-two come from the invented beat sheet on the Illustrative-data slide (its notes: the example film and its beat lengths are invented); naming a real course game, Walker Jumpman, without saying so presents invented timings as a real film's.
